  "rationale": "The BOOK ENTRY's core identification—that the great fish/sea-monster is a devouring ruler (Pharaoh, Nebuchadnezzar, Caesar) who swallows through the kingdom he heads and is forced to disgorge—directly matches the chapter's explicit derivation from the cited texts and the typological parallel to the Passion. The chapter grounds this in the sea-as-peoples motif, the ruler-as-head grammar (Dan 7), and the swallowing language (Jer 51:34,44; Ezek 29:3; 32:2), showing the fish as the appointed agent of imperial power in the sign of Jonah. support_scope.description: Support for the exact glossary BOOK ENTRY only, never for the supporting chapter as a whole.

book_secondary_elaborations.description: Secondary assertions actually printed in the glossary BOOK ENTRY; exclude chapter-only claims.

unsupported_glossary_assertions.description: Material assertions actually printed in the BOOK ENTRY that the evidence does not support. Must be empty for FULL and nonempty for CORE_ONLY.

chapter_only_objections.description: Objections to applications or arguments found only in the supporting chapter. Preserved for later chapter review and excluded from the glossary scope ruling.
